no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

builder-criteria.why: expect line 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 not quoted word for word in the builder brief: "`printf 'a\\tb\\n1\\t2\\n' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv` prints exactly `[{\"a\":\"1\",\""

words-only.why: I checked each of the seven verifier checks against its expect line. Checks 1–5 pass only if `cmp` finds a byte-for-byte match with the exact output plus a newline. Check 1 also requires exit=0, which its expect line asks for. Checks 2–5 add no exit-status test, which matches their wording. Check 5 uses `printf '%s\n'` with single quotes, so the expected text keeps the literal \t escape. That is exactly what the line requires, nothing more. Check 6 needs "npm test reports exit=0" and a test that runs bin/csv2json.js with --tsv on tab input and "asserts on the output". This matches "checks its output". Check 7 needs README.md to describe --tsv and give an example command line using it, which matches the line. The stricter items sit under "Advisory (not part of PASS or FAIL)": `npm run test:cli`, the exact `node bin/csv2json.js --tsv < file` form and wording, and the flag-position and parse.js checks. No PASS or FAIL condition goes beyond the expect line's words.

runs-as-written.why: I checked every command in both briefs. Every file they name exists at this commit: bin/csv2json.js, test/*.js, README.md and package.json. The builder's `npm run test:cli` works because the builder adds that script in step 4, before it is run. In the verifier brief, `npm run test:cli` only runs "if package.json defines that script". The printf/pipe/cmp commands are valid bash, and `cmp - <(printf '%s\n' ...)` uses bash process substitution. Check 5 uses `printf '%s\n' '[{"a\tb":"1\t2"}]'`, which keeps the backslash-t literal, so it matches JSON.stringify output. Check 1 sends output to /tmp/c1.out and reports `$?` from node, the last command in the pipeline, before the cmp step. The `grep -n -- '--tsv' test/*.js` arguments are valid. The JavaScript `execFileSync('node', ['bin/csv2json.js', '--tsv'], { input: ..., encoding: 'utf8' })` is valid. I found no command that would fail as written.

catches-traps.why:
Both must_catch items are handled.

Item 1: The builder brief names test/csv.test.js under "Current state". Step 3 says "Keep the existing tests", and step 4 requires confirming that `npm test` exits 0, which runs csv.test.js. Together these make the existing CSV tests something that must keep passing. The brief also protects the CSV path directly: "otherwise call parse(text) exactly as today" and "Do not change src/parse.js unless you have to". Step 2 adds byte-for-byte checks of no-flag CSV output.

Item 2: Verifier Check 6 runs "`npm test; echo \"exit=$?\"`", as the line says, and bases PASS/FAIL on that. `npm run test:cli` appears only under "Advisory (not part of PASS or FAIL)", with a note to record if the script isn't defined.

The builder brief's addition of a test:cli script is not covered by either must_catch item.

avoids-must-not.why: I checked both briefs against the two must_not items. (1) Verifier Check 6 bases PASS/FAIL on `npm test; echo "exit=$?"` and the grep plus reading of the test, not on `npm run test:cli`. The only mention of test:cli is in the Advisory section, which is explicitly "not part of PASS or FAIL". The builder brief asks for a test:cli script, but that is a builder step, not a verifier check. (2) The builder brief never asks for a general separator option. It says "Do not add --help, --sep/--delimiter, auto-detection..." and only adds the --tsv check on process.argv. Neither forbidden item appears anywhere in the output.

methods-private.why: The criterion holds. I compared the builder brief against the verifier's checks. Builder step 2 lists the five printf commands with their expected outputs. Those commands and outputs come straight from expect lines 1–5, which the criterion allows. The verifier's own probes are different: they wrap the output in `cmp - <(printf '%s\n' ...)`, compare it to a saved file, and look for "SAME". None of that appears in the builder brief. The builder brief also has no PASS/FAIL wording and doesn't include the verifier's `grep -n -- '--tsv' test/*.js` step. Step 3 tells the builder to write its own tests, which is allowed. Step 4 names `npm test` and `npm run test:cli`, both commands named in the expect lines and proofs, so that is allowed too. Step 5's README guidance repeats the proof 7 wording rather than any verifier condition. The note that `\t` is the two-character JSON escape clarifies the expect line and is not a check.
